statement: The point P(4, negative 2) is reflected in the y-axis. Its image is then reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of the final point?

choices.misconception: I did the reflection in the y-axis and forgot to do the second reflection.
I skipped the reflection in the y-axis and only reflected in the line y = x.
I did the two reflections in the opposite order, y = x first and then the y-axis.
I thought reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of both coordinates, which is really a half turn, and then swapped them.

hints: Do the two reflections one at a time, in order.
Know the rule for each mirror: reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of the first coordinate only, and reflecting in the line y = x swaps the two coordinates.
The first reflection gives (negative 4, negative 2). Now swap the two coordinates.

solutions.reliable: Reflecting (4, negative 2) in the y-axis keeps the second coordinate and changes the sign of the first, giving (negative 4, negative 2). Reflecting that in the line y = x swaps the coordinates, giving (negative 2, negative 4). The transferable idea: learn each reflection as a rule on coordinates, and apply a chain of transformations strictly in the order given, because order matters.

whyOnTest: Combined transformations test both the coordinate rules and the order, and each distractor is one rule or one step done wrongly.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
